query: How does resolution time vary across issue themes, channel, and priority?

per_column.name: issue_theme
per_column.rationale: Directly realises the 'issue themes' dimension of the query. Categories (functionality, performance, billing, integration, etc.) are interpretable and well-separated, with balanced counts allowing meaningful grouping of resolution_minutes across themes.

per_column.name: urgency_and_blocker_status
per_column.rationale: An associational segmentation (user_friction, customer_blocked, high_impact_outage, revenue_risk) that is external to resolution time and interpretable. It plausibly correlates with resolution_minutes and offers a distinct lens from the existing 'priority' column, supporting exploratory comparison.

per_column.name: issue_type
per_column.rationale: A finer taxonomy (bug_functionality, bug_performance, infrastructure_outage, api_auth_error, etc.) with interpretable, well-separated categories and reasonable counts. Overlaps somewhat with issue_theme but adds actionable granularity for segmenting resolution time; not a restatement of the focus.

judge.rationale: All three columns are external categorical variables with interpretable, well-separated categories and adequately balanced value distributions, enabling grouped comparison of resolution_minutes. issue_theme squarely addresses the requested 'issue themes' axis; urgency_and_blocker_status adds an orthogonal severity lens beyond the existing priority; issue_type offers finer bug/feature/infrastructure segmentation. issue_theme and issue_type partially overlap semantically, slightly reducing the incremental information as a set, but none restate the focus and none are near-constant or opaque scores. Strong support for discovering interpretable relationships.
